risk_flags.description: The contract should explicitly treat docs/requirements.md as the authority, not just implementation files. If code or other docs disagree with the requirements, documenting the code behavior could still produce incorrect customer-facing documentation.
risk_flags.span: Every factual claim in the new entries is verifiable against the actual code (cli.py, report.py, rates.py, config.py) or existing docs — nothing invented

risk_flags.description: Keeping every existing FAQ entry unchanged is risky unless the agent first confirms the free-tier limit still matches pricing.md. The project rules make FAQ/pricing consistency mandatory, so an existing mismatch cannot be preserved.
risk_flags.span: docs/faq.md retains all four existing entries unchanged

verdict.primary_risk: The main risk is that the contract may preserve or add FAQ content that is verifiable against code or existing text but not against docs/requirements.md, the project's source of truth.
